answer: terrace admits a cedar only by burning crystal equal to the square of the live cedar count; crystal is minted solely by judged work on that terrace and cannot be bought, sold or transferred. The count is read and incremented atomically at anchor, so a thousand-clone flood must complete judged work worth about 333 million crystal, each clone's bill attached to its anchor. Parallel workers cannot pool crystal, and splitting across terraces fails because terrace is one global registry. It breaks if crystal transfers, work is judged off-chain, or terrace shards.
